speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; to begin our assessment of your newborn, how long have they been born, and are there any specific symptoms or concerns you have noticed?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, are there any signs of jaundice, respiratory distress, or feeding difficulties? Did the umbilical cord fall off normally, or do you notice any unusual redness or swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The constellation of a continuous heart murmur (likely a patent ductus arteriosus), bluish macules on the skin (likely purpura fulminans or a manifestation of the rash), cloudy lenses (cataracts), and hearing loss represents the classic triad of congenital rubella syndrome (blueberry muffin rash, cataracts, and deafness) combined with cardiac defects.
